newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares close higher for second straight day.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares close higher for second straight day.

text.p: ** (1340 GMT) - Bombay blue chips close with modest gains
after tame start; market seen bottoming out, dealers say
** Bombay's benchmark index up 32.01 points, or 0.77 pct,
at 4,186.29 -- just off day's best level
** Foreign funds seek value in top blue chips, market mood
** Short-covering by operators on last day of weekly trade
at National Stock Exchange pushes up share prices
** Delhi index closes 14.34 pts up at 879.95, Madras falls
2.16 pts to 4,231.90, Calcutta down 0.12 pts at 127.0.
National exchange index up 8.25 pts at 1,173.25
Indian stocks shrugged off a lacklustre start on Tuesday, striding to a firmer close as foreign funds bought on expectations of the market bottoming out at current levels, traders said.
"There has been good fund buying in refinery, auto and oil stocks," said Ajay Srinivasan, Chief Investment Officer at ITC-Threadneedle Asset Management.
"The (broader) market has shown very impressive breadth and there has been a move in smaller stocks."
Last week shares fell victim to profit-taking and concern about the stability of the crisis-racked coalition government.
